add-to-event-alternatives-party-bar-hire.intro: This page is published by FireFlair, which runs FF Party. Facts about other services come from their own public pages, checked on 7 November 2026. Each route below can suit a different host, and what a page does not mention is not evidence that a service lacks it.
body: The main routes

| Route | How it works, per its public pages | May suit you if |
|---|---|---|
| **Add to Event** | You request quotes and compare suppliers, reviews and photos. Suppliers buy credits to contact selected leads and pay no booking commission. | You want several quotes and are happy to compare them yourself. |
| **Poptop** | Offers instant quotes for relevant services, deposit payment and supplier confirmation. Its help pages describe a supplier fee. | You want visible prices and an online deposit. An instant quote and a confirmed booking are different stages. |
| **Togather** | Matches an event brief with suppliers, with quotes, messaging and payment support. | You want a brief-led, curated route. |
| **Bark** | A broad services marketplace. Professionals pay credits to contact leads, and customers compare profiles and reviews. | You want a broad marketplace for many kinds of service. |
| **Direct bar companies** | Examples include Mix & Twist, Cocktailhire, Hire A Barman and Cocktail Barmen, who publish their own packages. | You know what you want and prefer a single specialist operator. |
| **FF Party** | You describe the event, choose professionals to invite, and see the professional's pay and FireFlair's booking charge separately. For a mobile bar or full package, the FireFlair team approaches suitable bartenders and bar companies for your brief and passes on who is available. | You want to pick the person, see the terms before committing, and have someone in events do the first round of enquiries. FF Party is young and does not list every company, so the options depend on who replies for your date. |
How to choose
Use the same criteria for each: service type, team, menu, supplies, total cost and how a booking is confirmed. The [comparison worksheet](/stories/how-to-compare-mobile-bar-companies) lays them out.

bartender-hire-vs-mobile-bar-hire.title: Bartender hire vs mobile bar hire
bartender-hire-vs-mobile-bar-hire.seo: Bartender hire vs mobile bar hire: which do you need?
bartender-hire-vs-mobile-bar-hire.blurb: Bartender hire usually supplies the person serving drinks, with the exact tools and extras set out in the booking. Mobile bar hire may also include the bar structure, staff, equipment...
bartender-hire-vs-mobile-bar-hire.intro: Bartender hire usually supplies the person serving drinks, with the exact tools and extras set out in the booking. Mobile bar hire may also include the bar structure, staff, equipment and drinks, depending on the package. Start with what your venue already provides, then compare the remaining responsibilities and the full price.
body: Decide from your own setup

| Your situation | Likely fit | Check |
|---|---|---|
| You have a usable counter or kitchen worktop, fridge space and water | A bartender | Who brings tools, glassware and ice |
| You have the space but no bar or equipment | Staff plus equipment, or a staffed mobile bar | What the bar needs: floor space, access, power if the supplier specifies it |
| You want one team to handle everything | A full bar package | What the package includes and excludes |
| You want to supply your own drinks | A bartender, or a supplier that offers it | Venue rules and supplier terms: see [supplying your own alcohol](/stories/supply-own-alcohol-hire-bartender) |
Why suppliers describe things differently

Some suppliers publish separate staff-only, staffed-bar and stocked-package options, and others quote around your brief. Terms such as "dry hire" are used in different ways, so read the inclusions rather than the label. See [dry bar hire explained](/stories/dry-bar-hire-staffed-bar-full-bar-service).
When one specialist operator makes sense

A direct mobile bar company can suit a host who wants a single point of contact and a complete, tailored service. A booking platform can suit a host who wants to choose a person and see exactly what is paid for. Neither is better in every case.

ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds.title: How FF Party booking deposits and refunds work
ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds.seo: FF Party booking charge and refunds explained
ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds.blurb: FF Party uses one £50 FireFlair booking charge for each Event Card, separate from the professional's pay. A request cancelled before anyone is confirmed qualifies for the applicable...
ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds.intro:
FF Party uses one £50 FireFlair booking charge for each Event Card, separate from the professional's pay. A request cancelled before anyone is confirmed qualifies for the applicable refund. Partly staffed events are reviewed individually. Check the current booking terms for the exact conditions that apply to your request.

The £50 is FireFlair's first-year launch price, and FireFlair has said it will stay fixed for loyal users.
body: Which money is which?

| Money | Who it is for | Covered by this guide? |
|---|---|---|
| FireFlair booking charge, £50 per Event Card | FireFlair, for running the booking | Yes |
| Professional's pay | The bartender or other professional, shown separately | No |
| Drinks, ingredients, equipment, travel | Depends on the service you choose | No |

Example, for illustration only and not a quotation: a bartender's pay of £100 plus the £50 FireFlair charge gives £150. Real pay depends on the shift, and many events need more than one position.

The charge is for the event, not for each person. An Event Card with several positions still carries one £50 charge.
When is the charge refunded?

- **Nothing secured.** If no professional is confirmed for the event, the applicable full refund applies.
- **Cancelled before confirmation.** Use "Cancel request & refund" before anyone is confirmed.
- **Partly staffed.** If some positions are filled and others are not, FireFlair reviews the event individually under the policy. There is no published formula that splits the charge by position.
- **Your bartender cancels.** The position is reopened and a replacement is sought through the agreed process, with no second replacement-matching charge. A replacement depends on availability.
What about cancelling or changing the date after you are confirmed?

Not sure of your date? You can still book, and change it later.

- **30 days or more before the event:** if you cancel or move the event, your booking charge can be used towards your next event.
- **Within 30 days of the event, once your staff are confirmed:** the charge is not refunded. This protects the professionals who have kept the date free for you.

The professional's cancellation pay is a separate matter from FireFlair's charge. These rules apply to FF Party events, so read them alongside the current booking terms.
Where is the record?

Your booking page on the website is the official record. WhatsApp and email carry notifications.

Related: [How to book a bartender on FF Party](/stories/how-to-book-a-bartender-on-ff-party) · [How much does it cost to hire a bartender?](/stories/how-much-does-it-cost-to-hire-a-bartender)

how-many-bartenders-do-i-need.title: How many bartenders do I need for my party?
how-many-bartenders-do-i-need.seo: How many bartenders do I need for 30, 50 or 100 guests?
how-many-bartenders-do-i-need.blurb: A planning guide, not a rule. The right number depends on how complicated your menu is, how many guests arrive at once, and whether anyone helps with glasses and ice. The examples below...
how-many-bartenders-do-i-need.intro: A planning guide, not a rule. The right number depends on how complicated your menu is, how many guests arrive at once, and whether anyone helps with glasses and ice. The examples below show the reasoning, with every assumption stated so you can change it.
body: What pushes the number up

- **A cocktail menu** takes longer per drink than beer, wine or a short list of simple mixed drinks.
- **A peak.** Guests arriving together, or a toast, create a queue that a quiet evening does not.
- **Short service windows.** A two-hour welcome drinks service is busier than a five-hour party.
- **No support.** A bartender who also fetches ice and clears glasses serves fewer drinks.
- **Layout.** Two service points halve the walking but need two people.
Worked examples (illustrative)

| Event | Assumptions | Planning idea |
|---|---|---|
| 30 guests, house party, 4 hours | Short cocktail list, steady arrivals, host helps with glasses | One experienced bartender |
| 50 guests, birthday, 4 hours | Cocktail list, most arrive within the first hour | One bartender plus support, or two bartenders if the list is long |
| 100 guests, reception, 3 hours | Mixed menu, drinks request at the same time | Two bartenders at least, with a glass and ice runner |

These are starting points for a conversation with the bartender you invite. They are planning estimates and are not guaranteed to suit your event.
How to plan it

1. Choose the drinks you will offer. See [how to plan a cocktail menu](/stories/how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party).
2. Decide the busiest hour and how many guests will want a drink in it.
3. Decide who helps with ice and glasses.
4. Request positions on your Event Card. Each position is invited and confirmed separately.

For a corporate event, see [staffing a product launch or drinks reception](https://ffstaff.uk/stories/staffing-a-product-launch-or-drinks-reception).

how-much-does-it-cost-to-hire-a-bartende.title: How much does it cost to hire a bartender?
how-much-does-it-cost-to-hire-a-bartende.seo: How much does it cost to hire a bartender in the UK?
how-much-does-it-cost-to-hire-a-bartende.blurb: The price depends on what is included. A bartender alone, a bartender with ingredients, a staffed mobile bar and a fully stocked package are different services, so compare what each...
how-much-does-it-cost-to-hire-a-bartende.intro: The price depends on what is included. A bartender alone, a bartender with ingredients, a staffed mobile bar and a fully stocked package are different services, so compare what each quote covers before comparing totals. Published prices are starting points set by each supplier, and no single figure can stand for the UK.
body: What changes the total

- **Hours of service**, including setup and clearing, not only the time guests are drinking.
- **Number of staff.** A larger or busier party needs more than one person. See [how many bartenders you need](/stories/how-many-bartenders-do-i-need).
- **Skills.** Classic cocktails, flair and a plain bar service are different jobs.
- **Equipment**, such as a bar, tools, glassware and ice.
- **Ingredients and alcohol**, and who supplies them.
- **Travel, delivery and parking.**
- **Minimum spend or minimum hours.**
- **VAT**, where the supplier charges it.
Ask every supplier the same questions

1. Is this the person only, the person with equipment, or a full package?
2. Are ingredients, ice and glassware included?
3. What is the minimum booking, and does travel cost extra?
4. Is VAT included in the price I am shown?
5. How is my booking confirmed, and what happens if the bartender cannot attend?

The [supplies checklist](/stories/what-to-provide-when-hiring-a-bartender) turns this into a list for your own venue.
Where FireFlair's charge fits

On FF Party the professional's pay and FireFlair's booking charge are shown separately. The charge is £50 for each Event Card, as a first-year launch price that FireFlair says will stay fixed for loyal users. For illustration only, and not a quotation: £100 pay plus the £50 charge is £150. The pay for a real shift depends on the hours, skills and number of people. See [how deposits and refunds work](/stories/ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds).
Why a flat booking charge matters

Many agencies and staffing platforms charge in proportion to the hours worked, either as an hourly rate or as a percentage of pay. As a worked example (invented, to show the arithmetic): if a bartender earns £20 an hour and an agency bills the client £40 an hour, a 10-hour shift costs the client £400, of which the bartender receives £200. The difference pays for the agency's costs, which can include payroll, insurance and administration, so it is not all profit.

FF Party works differently. The booking charge is fixed for the event, so a one-hour booking and a ten-hour booking carry the same FireFlair charge, and the professional's pay is shown on its own line. The same example on FF Party: £20 an hour for 10 hours is £200 pay, plus the £50 charge, which is £250. Pay is agreed with the professional, and your total depends on the hours you choose.
Supplier examples (checked 7 November 2026)

These are what each supplier or platform advertises. They are not a UK average, and they cover different things, so read the "includes" column.

| Source | Advertised price | What it describes |
|---|---|---|
| Poptop, London bartender listings | "From £120 per event"; individual listings from £210 and £270 per event | Platform listings for bartenders in London; the final price depends on guests, hours and menu |
| Poptop, UK cocktail bars | £33 per guest for all-inclusive drinks packages; around £325 per event for dry-hire cash bars (platform-reported averages) | Cocktail bar suppliers on the platform |
| BarOpsCo, London | £160 for bartender hire up to 3 hours; £300 for a cocktail bartender with setup up to 4 hours | One supplier's price guide; alcohol supplied by client or supplier |
| The Sesh Bars, London | Dry hire from £350; all-inclusive £6.50 to £7.50 per person per hour, excluding VAT | Bar, bartenders and glassware for dry hire; travel included inside the M25 |
| Mix & Twist, 2026 guide | £20 to £90 per head for mobile bars, standard service £20 to £50 | A mobile bar company's rough guide across styles |

Poptop's pages also show platform-wide averages that differ greatly between pages, so they are not used here. Check each supplier's current page, VAT and minimums before relying on any figure.

how-to-book-a-bartender-on-ff-party.title: How to book a bartender on FF Party
how-to-book-a-bartender-on-ff-party.seo: How to book a bartender on FF Party: step by step
how-to-book-a-bartender-on-ff-party.blurb: You describe your event, pay FireFlair's booking charge, and FF Party invites bartenders who fit. A booking is confirmed only when a bartender accepts, or when you choose one who has...
how-to-book-a-bartender-on-ff-party.intro: You describe your event, pay FireFlair's booking charge, and FF Party invites bartenders who fit. A booking is confirmed only when a bartender accepts, or when you choose one who has said they are available. Until then you have a request, not a booking.
body: What you need before you start
Your phone number and email, the date, place, start and finish times, guest numbers, and the kind of service you want. You do not need a company account.
The steps

1. **Describe the event.** Occasion, guests, hours and location. The event is saved as an Event Card.
2. **Say what you need.** Each role you need becomes a Shift Card on the event, such as one bartender or two. Each position is tracked separately.
3. **Pay FireFlair's booking charge.** It is taken before invitations go out and is separate from the bartender's pay, which is shown on its own line.
4. **Invite.** You can invite a bartender by name, which is an exclusive invitation, or let Autofill invite a batch of matching professionals.
5. **Choose and confirm.** See "What happens next" below.
What happens next

**Exclusive invitation.** The bartender you chose has up to 24 hours to reply, and never beyond the start of the shift. They can accept and confirm, decline, or ask a question. If they accept, the booking is confirmed without a second approval from you. The invitation is exclusive for that shift. It does not reserve their whole diary.

**Autofill.** Invitations go to a batch of matching professionals, normally ten. "Available" is a reply, not a confirmation: you then pick the person you want. Choosing "Discuss first" does not confirm anything and does not extend any deadline. Each invitation has its own selection deadline, normally the earlier of seven days after it was created and the start of the shift. A reply does not restart those seven days.
Does 24 hours mean I get an answer in 24 hours?

No. It is the time a bartender has to respond. It is not a promise of a reply or of a confirmed booking within a day. If you are booking close to the date, say so in the request and keep a second option in mind.
After you are confirmed

You both receive the booking details and the supported contact information. Your booking page on the website is the official record; WhatsApp and email carry notifications and quick replies. You can leave a review on the website after the event.
If something changes

If a confirmed bartender cancels, the position is reopened and a replacement is sought through the same process, with no further replacement-matching charge. A replacement depends on availability. For refunds, see [how FF Party booking deposits and refunds work](/stories/ff-party-booking-deposits-and-refunds).
Which guide next?

- Working out your numbers: [How many bartenders do I need for my party?](/stories/how-many-bartenders-do-i-need)
- Choosing a service type: [Bartender hire vs mobile bar hire](/stories/bartender-hire-vs-mobile-bar-hire)
- Drinks: [How to plan a cocktail menu for a party](/stories/how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party)

Professionals who want to be invited can [build a bartender profile on FF Team](https://ffteam.uk/stories/how-to-build-a-bartender-profile).

how-to-compare-mobile-bar-companies.title: How to compare mobile bar companies
how-to-compare-mobile-bar-companies.seo: How to compare mobile bar companies: a worksheet
how-to-compare-mobile-bar-companies.blurb: Quotes only compare fairly when each company is pricing the same thing. Write down your event first, then ask each company to answer the same eight questions. The worksheet below does...
how-to-compare-mobile-bar-companies.intro: Quotes only compare fairly when each company is pricing the same thing. Write down your event first, then ask each company to answer the same eight questions. The worksheet below does that, and leaves the decision with you.
body: The worksheet

| Question | Company A | Company B | Company C |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Service:** staff only, staff and equipment, or full package? | | | |
| **Team:** how many people, what experience, who supervises? | | | |
| **Menu:** fixed list, or tailored? Alcohol-free options included? | | | |
| **Supplies:** who provides alcohol, ingredients, ice, glassware? | | | |
| **Setup:** space, access, power and water the company needs from you | | | |
| **Travel and delivery:** included or extra? | | | |
| **Total cost:** hours, equipment, ingredients, travel, VAT, minimum spend | | | |
| **Confirmation:** when is it confirmed, who tells you, what are the cancellation and replacement terms? | | | |
Quote, deposit and confirmed booking are different stages

Platforms and companies handle these differently. Some show an instant quote, some ask you to wait for a supplier to confirm, some take a deposit first. Note which stage you are at before you assume the date is secure.
Evidence to look for

Real photographs of the company's own events, reviews you can trace to a platform, and a clear description of who will actually attend. Treat unattributed claims such as "the best in the area" as marketing.
Where FF Party fits

FF Party lets you describe the event, choose the people you want to invite, and see the professional's pay and FireFlair's booking charge separately.

You do not have to search the whole market yourself. FF Party is a young network, and it does not claim to list every bar company. If you need a mobile bar or a full package, tell us what you want. The FireFlair team works in events, and we contact bartenders and bar companies that look suited to your brief and pass on who is available. What you can compare depends on who replies for your date and area, and we do not promise a set number of options.

For other routes, see [Add to Event alternatives for party bar hire](/stories/add-to-event-alternatives-party-bar-hire).

how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party.title: How to plan a cocktail menu for a party
how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party.seo: How to plan a cocktail menu for a party
how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party.blurb: Pick a short list that covers the main tastes, keeps the bartender's work manageable and includes good alcohol-free choices. Three to five different drinks is the sweet spot. More choice...
how-to-plan-a-cocktail-menu-for-a-party.intro: Pick a short list that covers the main tastes, keeps the bartender's work manageable and includes good alcohol-free choices. Three to five different drinks is the sweet spot. More choice slows service for everyone.
body: A balanced list

- **One long, refreshing drink** that works as the default, such as a highball or spritz style.
- **One classic with a spirit-led flavour**, for guests who like a stronger drink.
- **One sweeter or fruitier option.**
- **One bitter or dry option**, if your guests will enjoy it.
- **At least one alcohol-free cocktail**, treated as a drink and not an afterthought.
Keep the service realistic

Drinks that are shaken, stirred or built over ice each take different amounts of time, and the more elaborate drinks slow a queue. If you expect a rush, keep most of the menu to quick builds and offer one or two showpiece drinks. This is also why [the number of bartenders](/stories/how-many-bartenders-do-i-need) depends on the menu.
Who supplies what

Decide with your supplier whether they bring the ingredients, you do, or the cost is shared. See [what to provide when you hire a bartender](/stories/what-to-provide-when-hiring-a-bartender) and [supplying your own alcohol](/stories/supply-own-alcohol-hire-bartender).
Using the FF Party menu

The FF Party cocktail menu opens with the UK's best-loved classics, and you tap a card to see the recipe. A switch shows mocktails, which work the same way.

- **Add favourites.** Save the drinks you love, and they are remembered for next time.
- **Say how many servings.** Quantities are set in servings, in steps of 20, and your bartender can talk the numbers through with you.
- **Recipes on your invoice.** The invoice lists each cocktail with its full recipe scaled to your servings, so your professionals see what you expect.
- **Tips and requests.** Add anything special on the request box. It appears on your Event Card and invoice.
- **Rebook the same drinks.** Your choices stay with you, so booking another party can start from the same cocktails.

Ask the bartender to confirm what they can make before the event.

what-to-provide-when-hiring-a-bartender.title: What do I need to provide when I hire a bartender?

what-to-provide-when-hiring-a-bartender.blurb: It depends on the package. Suppliers publish different inclusions: some supply only the person, some add ingredients, equipment or a bar. Use the checklist below and mark each line as...

body: Responsibility checklist

| Item | Me | Bartender or supplier | Agreed |

| Mixers, juices, garnishes and other ingredients | | | |

| Water, and a place to wash up | | | |

| Alcohol-free options | | | |
| Setup time before guests arrive | | | |

Questions that avoid surprises

- If I supply the drinks, who decides quantities? See [supplying your own alcohol](/stories/supply-own-alcohol-hire-bartender).
- Is setup time part of the paid hours?
- What happens to leftovers?

bar-staffing-agency-or-freelance-platfor.title: Bar staffing agency or freelance bartender platform
bar-staffing-agency-or-freelance-platfor.seo: Bar staffing agency or freelance bartender platform: which to use
bar-staffing-agency-or-freelance-platfor.blurb: A managed agency usually supplies and manages the staff for you. A freelance platform lets you choose from individual professionals. FireFlair connects you with professionals and handles...
bar-staffing-agency-or-freelance-platfor.intro: A managed agency usually supplies and manages the staff for you. A freelance platform lets you choose from individual professionals. FireFlair connects you with professionals and handles the booking, and the pay and working arrangement are agreed between you and each professional. Your choice depends on how much choosing, managing and responsibility you want.
body: What differs

| | Managed agency | Freelance platform |
|---|---|---|
| **Who selects** | The agency, to your brief | You, from profiles, or the platform matches |
| **Support** | Often a named account contact and cover | Varies by platform |
| **Payroll and pay** | Often handled by the agency | Varies; some platforms handle payment, others leave it to you |
| **Cost shape** | May be an hourly client rate | May be a percentage fee, or a fixed charge per booking |
| **Responsibility** | Depends on the arrangement | Depends on the arrangement |

Employment status and liability depend on the actual working arrangement, not on what a contract calls it. Check current Acas and government guidance, or take advice, before you rely on any one model.
When an agency may fit

- You need a large team or multiple events at once.
- You want a single contact who takes responsibility for supply.
- You want payroll and compliance handled for you.

Examples include general hospitality agencies and bar specialists such as Off to Work, Wilde Toast, Viking Staffing & Events and Flair.
When a platform may fit

- You want to see and choose individuals.
- You want to rebook the same people.
- You want costs that are clear up front.
How FF Staff works

You build the brief, pay a fixed booking charge for each Shift Card, and invite the people you want. See [how to book bar staff on FF Staff](/stories/how-to-book-bar-staff-on-ff-staff). FF Staff is young and does not promise coverage in every area or on every date.

ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacemen.title: How FF Staff booking fees, refunds and replacements work
ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacemen.seo: FF Staff booking fees, refunds and replacements explained
ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacemen.blurb: FF Staff charges £10 for each Shift Card, paid before invitations are sent. It is not £10 per person and not £10 per hour. The professional's pay is separate. Unfilled Shift Cards are...
ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacemen.intro: FF Staff charges £10 for each Shift Card, paid before invitations are sent. It is not £10 per person and not £10 per hour. The professional's pay is separate. Unfilled Shift Cards are refunded under the policy, and partly filled cards are reviewed. This is first-year launch pricing, which FireFlair says will stay fixed for loyal users. Check the current booking terms for the exact conditions.
body: What is charged

| Item | Charge |
|---|---|
| FireFlair booking charge | £10 per Shift Card |
| Professional's pay | Agreed with each professional and shown separately |
| Autofill | No extra charge |

A Shift Card with several positions carries one charge. Separate Shift Cards for different roles carry a charge each.
Refunds

- **Before you confirm anyone:** use Cancel request & refund.
- **Nobody found, or the time to choose ran out:** the charge for that Shift Card is refunded.
- **Several cards:** each is treated separately. You keep the charge for the cards filled and are refunded for those that are not.
- **Part-filled card:** a Shift Card asking for several people where only some are found is reviewed individually. There is no published per-person formula.
- **After you and the professional have both confirmed:** if you cancel, the booking charge is not refunded. Pay or cancellation payments owed to the professional are agreed between you and them.
Replacements

If a confirmed professional cancels, the position is reopened and a replacement is sought through the agreed process, with no further replacement-matching charge. A replacement depends on availability. If a replacement cannot be found, the charge for the unfilled position is handled under the policy.
The record

The website is the official record. WhatsApp and email carry notifications.

how-to-book-bar-staff-on-ff-staff.title: How to book bar staff on FF Staff
how-to-book-bar-staff-on-ff-staff.seo: How to book bar staff on FF Staff: a worked example
how-to-book-bar-staff-on-ff-staff.blurb: You create an event, add a shift for each role, pay FireFlair's booking charge, then invite people by name or let Autofill find them. Someone is booked only when they accept and confirm,...
how-to-book-bar-staff-on-ff-staff.intro: You create an event, add a shift for each role, pay FireFlair's booking charge, then invite people by name or let Autofill find them. Someone is booked only when they accept and confirm, or when you choose a professional who has said they are available.
body: How the pieces fit

An Event Card holds your event. Each role you need is a Shift Card, and a Shift Card can ask for several professionals. Each position and each invitation is tracked separately. The minimum you need is a phone number, an email, the event and shift details, payment and acceptance of the terms. You do not need a company account first.
A worked example (fictional)

*A hotel needs a drinks reception on Friday 6pm to 11pm: three bartenders and one barback.*

1. Create the Event Card with the date, place and timings.
2. Add a Shift Card for bartenders and ask for three positions. Add a second Shift Card for the barback, which has a different role and pay.
3. Add duties, hours, pay, dress code and requirements.
4. Pay the booking charge for the two Shift Cards. It is taken before invitations go out. The pay for each professional is separate and agreed with them.
5. Choose people from the staff row, or choose Autofill.
Choose a person, or Autofill

**By name.** The person is invited exclusively for up to 24 hours, never beyond the shift start. If they choose Accept & confirm, the position is filled with no second approval.

**Autofill.** It invites professionals who match the role and work near you, normally ten at a time. Their reply "Available" is not a booking: you see who is available and any questions, then choose. Discuss first confirms nothing and does not extend a deadline.
How long you have to choose
Each invitation has its own deadline, normally the earlier of seven days after it was created and the shift start. A reply does not restart the seven days. Your booking page shows the real deadline.
After confirmation

You receive the booking reference, shift details, profile link and contact details. The website is the official record, and WhatsApp and email carry notifications. See [fees, refunds and replacements](/stories/ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacements) for what happens if something changes.

how-to-find-last-minute-bar-staff.title: How to find last-minute bar staff
how-to-find-last-minute-bar-staff.seo: How to find last-minute bar staff
how-to-find-last-minute-bar-staff.blurb: Send a complete brief at once, name the skills you cannot compromise on, invite several people in parallel, and treat anyone as booked only once they confirm. Speed comes from clear...
how-to-find-last-minute-bar-staff.intro: Send a complete brief at once, name the skills you cannot compromise on, invite several people in parallel, and treat anyone as booked only once they confirm. Speed comes from clear information, not from skipping steps.
body: Write the brief in five lines

1. Date, start and finish, and exact address.
2. Role and how many people.
3. Must-have skills, for example solo bar or classic cocktails.
4. Pay for the shift.
5. Who they meet and what they wear.

A complete brief gets faster answers because professionals do not need to ask. See [how to write a brief for temporary bar staff](/stories/temporary-bar-staff-brief-template).
Be realistic about timing

Professionals have up to 24 hours to reply to an invitation, and never beyond the shift start. That is a response window. It does not guarantee a reply or a confirmed booking within a day. For urgent shifts:

- Invite several matching professionals rather than waiting on one.
- Use Autofill alongside people you already know.
- Keep a backup plan until someone is confirmed.

Each invitation shows its real deadline, normally the earlier of seven days after creation and the shift start.
Check it is confirmed
"Available" is not a booking. You are covered only when a professional has accepted and confirmed, or when you have chosen them. Check your booking page, which is the official record.
If you cannot fill it

If nobody is confirmed, the unfilled Shift Card is refunded under the policy. See [fees, refunds and replacements](/stories/ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacements). If someone cancels, see [what to do when an event bartender cancels](/stories/what-to-do-when-an-event-bartender-cancels).

temporary-bar-staff-hire-cost.title: How much does it cost to hire temporary bar staff?
temporary-bar-staff-hire-cost.seo: How much does it cost to hire temporary bar staff?
temporary-bar-staff-hire-cost.blurb: The total is the professional's pay for the hours worked, plus any booking fee or agency charge, plus tax where it applies and costs such as travel. Different providers split these...
temporary-bar-staff-hire-cost.intro: The total is the professional's pay for the hours worked, plus any booking fee or agency charge, plus tax where it applies and costs such as travel. Different providers split these differently, so compare what each one charges and who pays what.
body: The cost components

- **Pay** for the shift, including setup and clear-down if you agree them.
- **Hours**, because pay and many fees grow with time.
- **Booking fee or agency charge**, and how it is calculated.
- **VAT, employer costs or payroll**, depending on the arrangement.
- **Travel, uniform or equipment**, if not included.
How providers charge

Providers use different structures. Brigad's pages describe a percentage service fee, with a separate fee for talent and for business. limber's pricing page describes a percentage fee on a plan, with wages and employment costs additional. An agency may bill an hourly client rate above the worker's pay. Because many of these grow with hours, a long shift costs more in fees as well as pay.

FF Staff charges a fixed booking charge per Shift Card, paid before invitations go out. It is not per person and not per hour, so a one-hour shift and a ten-hour shift carry the same charge. Pay for each professional is separate and agreed with them. This is first-year launch pricing, which FireFlair says will stay fixed for loyal users. VAT presentation will be shown at checkout.
Examples (fictional, to show the arithmetic)

| Booking | Pay | FireFlair charge | Total before VAT |
|---|---|---|---|
| One bartender, 6 hours at £20 an hour, one Shift Card | £120 | £10 | £130 |
| Three bartenders on one Shift Card, 5 hours each at £20 an hour | £300 | £10 | £310 |
| Three bartenders and one barback on two Shift Cards (barback at £15 an hour for 5 hours) | £375 | £20 | £395 |

Compare an hourly client rate of £40 for the same three bartenders over 5 hours, which would be £600 before any other cost. That rate also pays the agency's own costs, so the gap is not all profit. Check each provider's current terms.

See also: [Hospitality staffing fees and booking charges explained](/stories/hospitality-staffing-fees-explained) and [how fees, refunds and replacements work on FF Staff](/stories/ff-staff-booking-fees-refunds-replacements).

ff-team-vs-indeed-flex-for-bartenders.title: FF Team vs Indeed Flex for bartenders
ff-team-vs-indeed-flex-for-bartenders.seo: FF Team vs Indeed Flex for bartenders: compared
ff-team-vs-indeed-flex-for-bartenders.blurb: Indeed Flex offers temporary work across several sectors, including dedicated bartender roles. FF Team is being developed around bartenders' profiles, professional relationships and...
ff-team-vs-indeed-flex-for-bartenders.intro:
Indeed Flex offers temporary work across several sectors, including dedicated bartender roles. FF Team is being developed around bartenders' profiles, professional relationships and event bookings. The better fit depends on the work available near you, the payment arrangements you want, and how you prefer to present and build your professional reputation.

This page is published by FireFlair, which runs FF Team.
body: Side by side

| | Indeed Flex | FF Team |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | Temporary work across sectors, with a bartender route | Bartender-first, with other event professions |
| **Work found through** | Shifts posted by businesses, matching and returning-worker pools described on its employer pages | Invitations to you by name, or Autofill batches matched on role and distance |
| **Your public profile** | Not established from the pages checked | A shareable Profile Card with roles, work areas, reviews and connections |
| **Joining** | Onboarding and verification; check the current eligibility | Free profile |
| **Fees to you** | Check its current terms. Its key information document describes the agency-worker payment relationship | No percentage deducted from agreed professional pay. The booking charge is paid by the person booking |
| **Payment** | Includes a benefit called Instant Pay, subject to its terms | Professional pay is separate from the FireFlair charge and is arranged with the booker |
| **Commitment** | Flexible schedules | You accept or decline each invitation |
| **Maturity** | Established, large | New. FireFlair does not promise a number of shifts |
Who each may suit

**Indeed Flex** may suit you if you want a wide choice of shifts, an established process and agency-handled pay.

**FF Team** may suit you if you want your craft, reviews and connections visible on one profile, and want to build repeat bookings with the people who hire you.

Many bartenders use both. Compare the terms before you accept any shift, and read [what to check before accepting a bar shift](/stories/what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shift).

how-to-accept-bookings-on-ff-team.title: How to receive and accept bookings on FF Team
how-to-accept-bookings-on-ff-team.seo: How to accept bookings on FF Team: invitations explained
how-to-accept-bookings-on-ff-team.blurb: Every request arrives as a card with the role, duties, place, date, hours, pay and terms. If you are invited by name, you can accept and confirm, decline or ask a question. If it comes...
how-to-accept-bookings-on-ff-team.intro: Every request arrives as a card with the role, duties, place, date, hours, pay and terms. If you are invited by name, you can accept and confirm, decline or ask a question. If it comes from Autofill, replying "Available" tells the booker you are willing, and the booker then chooses.
body: Read the card first

The card shows what you need to decide: role, duties, location, date, hours, pay, dress code, requirements and terms. Requests arrive on WhatsApp and on your Bookings page. The website is the official record.
Two kinds of invitation

| | Invited by name (exclusive) | Autofill |
|---|---|---|
| Who gets it | You alone | A batch of matching professionals, normally ten |
| Your time to reply | Up to 24 hours, never beyond the shift start | Up to 24 hours |
| Accept & confirm | You are booked straight away, with no second approval | Not available |
| Available | Not needed | You tell the booker you can do it. You are **not** booked until they choose you |
| Discuss first | Ask a question. It does not confirm anything | Same. It does not extend any deadline |
| Decline | Frees the booker to invite someone else | Same |

Up to 24 hours is the time you have to reply. It is not a promise from FireFlair to answer you or confirm a booking within a day.
Ask before you commit
Use Discuss first to check things such as transport, duties or whether pay can change. Only a person at FireFlair can change the pay or terms shown on the card.
When you are confirmed
You and the booker receive the booking reference, shift details, profile links and the supported contact details. Your contact details are shared only once you are confirmed.
If you cannot make it
Open the booking and choose Cancel shift. FireFlair is told straight away and works to find a replacement. Cancel as early as you can, because the booker is relying on you.
After the event

Leave and receive reviews on the website. They become part of your profile and help you get booked again.

See also: [What to check before accepting a bar shift](/stories/what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shift)

how-to-build-a-bartender-profile.title: How to build a bartender profile that gets booked
how-to-build-a-bartender-profile.seo: How to build a bartender profile that gets booked
how-to-build-a-bartender-profile.blurb: A good profile answers a booker's questions in seconds: who you are, what you do, where you work and whether people trust you. Lead with a clear photo, list your roles in the words...
how-to-build-a-bartender-profile.intro: A good profile answers a booker's questions in seconds: who you are, what you do, where you work and whether people trust you. Lead with a clear photo, list your roles in the words clients search, show your work areas, and collect reviews after every event.
body: The structure that works

1. **A clear photo.** Bright, friendly, ideally you at work. Keep your face and head fully in frame.
2. **Your professions.** Use the titles people type: cocktail bartender, flair bartender, mixologist, bar manager, barback. See [the difference between a bartender, mixologist and flair bartender](/stories/bartender-mixologist-flair-bartender-difference).
3. **Where you work.** Add the areas you cover. Your Profile Card appears by area, never by your address.
4. **Evidence of skill.** Name what you can make and run: a classic menu, high-volume service, event setup, solo bars. Be specific and be honest.
5. **Reviews.** Ask the person who booked you to leave one after the event. A few good reviews do more than any description.
6. **Your people.** Add colleagues you have worked with. A connection means you know each other; it does not prove you worked a particular event together.
Example (fictional)

> **Sam R.** Cocktail bartender · Hertfordshire and north London
> Eight years in hotel and event bars. Classic cocktail menus, solo bar setup for up to 60 guests, alcohol-free menus. Travels with own tools. Can bring a barback by arrangement.

This is an invented example to show the level of detail. Do not copy it. Use your own facts.
Mistakes to avoid

- Claiming experience you cannot back up.
- Using a photo that hides your face or is cropped badly.
- Listing every possible role. A focused profile is easier to book.

Your public profile also works alongside a CV. See [how to write a bartender CV](/stories/how-to-write-a-bartender-cv).

[Create your profile](https://ffteam.uk)

how-to-find-freelance-bartending-work-uk.title: How to find freelance bartending work in the UK
how-to-find-freelance-bartending-work-uk.seo: How to find freelance bartending work in the UK
how-to-find-freelance-bartending-work-uk.blurb: Freelance bartending work comes through five routes: work platforms, staffing agencies, event bar companies, personal referrals and direct contact with venues. Most people use more than...
how-to-find-freelance-bartending-work-uk.intro: Freelance bartending work comes through five routes: work platforms, staffing agencies, event bar companies, personal referrals and direct contact with venues. Most people use more than one. Start with the route that fits how much control and commitment you want, then build a profile that makes you easy to book.
body: The five routes

| Route | How it works | Worth knowing |
|---|---|---|
| **Work platforms** | You join, set your availability and accept shifts. Examples include Indeed Flex (a dedicated bartender route), Brigad and Stint. | Check what each takes from your pay or charges the business, and what commitment it asks for. |
| **Staffing agencies** | An agency places you on shifts and usually handles pay. | Some hospitality agencies have a specialist bar division with bartenders, barbacks and flair roles. |
| **Event bar companies** | Companies that run bars at weddings, parties and corporate events book freelancers for busy dates. | Contact them directly and ask what they look for. |
| **Referrals** | Other bartenders, managers and past clients pass work on. | The strongest route. See [repeat bookings](/stories/repeat-bookings-freelance-bartender). |
| **Direct to venues** | You approach bars, hotels and venues for cover shifts. | Slower, and works best when you already know someone. |

Coople closed its UK operations from 1 January 2026, so if you used it before, see [Coople alternatives for UK bar staff](/stories/coople-alternatives-uk-bar-staff) when it is available, and contact Coople for old pay or tax paperwork.
What makes you bookable

- A clear profile with the roles you do, the areas you cover and honest photos. See [how to build a bartender profile](/stories/how-to-build-a-bartender-profile).
- Reviews and people who will vouch for you.
- Fast replies. A booking request often goes to the first person who answers.
- Clear terms before you accept. Use the [shift checklist](/stories/what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shift).
Where FF Team fits

FF Team starts with bartenders. You build a Profile Card that shows your craft, experience, work areas and the people you work with, and you can share it by link. Event hosts and businesses invite you to shifts, and you see the details before you commit. A free profile has no percentage taken from your agreed pay, and the booking charge is paid by the person booking.

FF Team does not promise a number of shifts. Work depends on demand in your area.

[Create your profile](https://ffteam.uk)

indeed-flex-alternatives-for-bartenders.title: Indeed Flex alternatives for bartenders in the UK
indeed-flex-alternatives-for-bartenders.seo: Indeed Flex alternatives for bartenders in the UK
indeed-flex-alternatives-for-bartenders.blurb: This page is published by FireFlair, which runs FF Team. It describes other services from their own public pages as checked on 7 November 2026. Indeed Flex is a large, established route...
indeed-flex-alternatives-for-bartenders.intro: This page is published by FireFlair, which runs FF Team. It describes other services from their own public pages as checked on 7 November 2026. Indeed Flex is a large, established route with a dedicated bartender section, so the aim here is to show what else exists and who each option may suit.
body: How this list was chosen

Services that advertise bar or hospitality work in the UK, that you can join as an individual, and whose pages describe how they work. Overseas-only services and services that have closed in the UK are left out.
The options

| Option | What its pages describe | May suit you if |
|---|---|---|
| **Indeed Flex** | Temporary work across sectors, a bartender route, flexible schedules, verification and benefits | You want broad choice of shifts and an established process. Check eligibility for benefits and how pay is handled |
| **Brigad** | Hospitality freelance missions, contracts, invoicing, payment options and insurance. A talent service fee is stated on its help page | You want the admin handled and have checked the fee and what it covers |
| **limber** | Hospitality staffing, favourite worker teams, payment and payroll handling | You want to be added to a business's regular team |
| **Stint** | Recurring short shifts in hospitality. Current help material describes a commitment of at least three months | You want regular, repeating shifts rather than one-offs |
| **Specialist bar agencies** | Dedicated bar divisions covering barbacks, bartenders, flair and managers, for example Off to Work and Wilde Toast | You want event bar work with a bar-focused team |
| **Event and festival staffing** | For example hap Solutions and Flair, covering festivals, stadiums and large events | You want large-event work. Check location and current vacancies |
| **FF Team** | A bartender-first profile, shareable by link, with invitations from event hosts and businesses | You want to show your craft, build repeat relationships and see the brief before you commit. It is new and does not promise shifts |

Coople closed its UK operations from 1 January 2026.
Questions to ask any of them

1. Who pays me, when, and what is taken from my pay?
2. How much commitment is required?
3. Do I choose my shifts?
4. Can I build a public profile or reputation?
5. Am I treated as self-employed or as a worker, and does that match the reality of the work? See [freelance or agency work](/stories/freelance-bartending-or-agency-bar-work).

For a direct comparison, see [FF Team vs Indeed Flex for bartenders](/stories/ff-team-vs-indeed-flex-for-bartenders).

what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shi.title: What to check before accepting a bar shift
what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shi.seo: What to check before accepting a bar shift: checklist
what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shi.blurb: Confirm the duties, the total hours including setup and clear-down, the rate, who pays you and when, how you get there and what happens if plans change. If the brief does not say, ask...
what-to-check-before-accepting-a-bar-shi.intro: Confirm the duties, the total hours including setup and clear-down, the rate, who pays you and when, how you get there and what happens if plans change. If the brief does not say, ask before you accept.
body: The checklist

| Check | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Duties** | Bar service only, or also barback work, stock, glass collection or setup? |
| **Total hours** | Do paid hours include setup and finish, or only service? |
| **Arrival time and place** | Access, parking, loading, who meets you |
| **Rate and who pays** | Is the pay per hour or for the shift? Who pays, you from the booker or an agency? |
| **Payment date and method** | When, how, and whether you invoice |
| **Breaks** | When and how long |
| **Uniform and kit** | What you wear and what you bring |
| **Menu** | Cocktail list or simple service? Can you learn it in time? |
| **Support** | Is there a barback or manager? Who is your contact on the night? |
| **Transport home** | Late finishes, last trains, paid taxi |
| **Cancellation** | What happens if the event is cancelled or you cannot attend |
Two sample briefs (fictional)

**Brief A: house party.** Saturday 7pm to midnight, home in Hertford, 40 guests, five classic cocktails supplied by host, 30 minutes setup, bring your own tools. Pay for the whole shift, paid by the host. *Questions to ask: is setup paid, who supplies ice and glassware, how do I get home?*

**Brief B: corporate drinks reception.** Thursday 6pm to 10pm, two bartenders and a barback, 120 guests, wine, beer and one signature drink, uniform provided, contact is the venue manager. Agency pays on the 15th of the following month. *Questions to ask: what is the rate, are breaks covered, what if the event ends early?*

On FF Team the card shows most of these. Use Discuss first for anything missing. See [how to accept bookings on FF Team](/stories/how-to-accept-bookings-on-ff-team).
